_comment: The e2e matrix: what must be true, separate from how it is checked.
'source' is a repo-relative file; 'generate' is a byte count filled with /dev/urandom.
'expect' is compared against facts read back from Postgres after the upload.
Every case additionally asserts the downloaded bytes are identical to the source.
Storage cases come from docs/erasure-coding.md: 1 = inline, 2 = whole block, 3 = 8+4 stripe.

cases.name: case1-inline-boundary
cases.why: 128KB minus one byte: the last size that still goes inline

cases.name: case2-block-boundary
cases.why: exactly 128KB: the first size that becomes a whole block chunk

cases.name: case2-real-image
cases.why: 930KB, the ordinary mid-size path, no erasure coding

cases.name: case3-stripe-plus-tail
cases.why: 40MB: one full 8+4 stripe plus an 8MB tail chunk

cases.name: case3-exact-block
cases.why: exactly 32MB. NOTE: docs/erasure-coding.md reads as Case 2 at this size, but a full block is a complete stripe and the code erasure-codes it. See docs/failure-catalog.md#boundary-32mb.

cases.name: case3-multi-stripe
cases.why: 68MB: two full stripes plus a 4MB tail, proving block indexing across stripes
